newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 2.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The labour movement has stepped up pressure on Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, hoping to force him to keep a controversial May Day pledge to raise the minimum wage by 20 baht a day. Cautiously welcoming the promise, labour leaders make it clear they will not tolerate future backtracking and dismiss the characteristically tongue-in-cheek manner in which the vow is delivered. (THE NATION)

- Air and noise pollution around Chitrlada Palace, the King's residence, is worsening, the city's surveys have found. Measurements of air and noise levels by monitoring stations around the palace have shown both to be higher than acceptable standards. The pollution is at its worst during morning and evening rush hours. (BANGKOK POST)

- The marathon protest of villagers rallying as the Assembly of the Poor will most likely end today as an agreement is expected on a final settlement package during a meeting with the prime minister. But the government is bracing for fresh protests which could drastically snowball. Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand workers were yesterday gathering at a plant, giving significant momentum to state enterprise workers' campaign against privatisation. (THE NATION)

- The Transport and Communications Ministry has finalised a framework for the establishment of a national shipping line, which it will submit to Cabinet this month. A group of Thai carriers will own no less than 51 percent of the national line while the rest will be held by customers including import/export companies, state enterprises, financial institutions, strategic partners and even state-run Thai Maritime Navigation. (THE NATION)

- The Board of Investment (BOI) is planning to introduce strategic and investment promotional measures to encourage increased Thai investment in Indochina, Burma, China, and members of the ASEAN grouping. BOI secretary-general says foreign investment values in those countries steadily increased during the period 1988 to 1996, especially in Laos and Burma. In fact, Thai investors were listed among top investors. (BUSINESS DAY)
